children: EchoStar Corp. (ECHO, Financials), the satellite and wireless communications company behind Dish Network, may offer investors an unusual way to gain exposure to SpaceX without buying SpaceX shares directly.

Morgan Stanley analyst Sean Diffley started coverage of EchoStar with a Buy rating and $134 price target, implying roughly 45% upside. His argument starts with a deal EchoStar struck with SpaceX last year.
EchoStar agreed to sell spectrum licenses to Elon Musk's space company for about $17 billion, split between as much as $8.5 billion in cash and $8.5 billion in SpaceX shares.
Morgan Stanley expects EchoStar to own about 262 million SpaceX shares, or roughly 2% of the company, once the transaction closes in November 2027. Here is where it gets interesting.
The bank estimates those shares could eventually be worth almost $40 billion. EchoStar itself is currently valued at roughly $27 billion.
Diffley believes that gap has become too wide to ignore. There are risks. Some EchoStar assets remain in bankruptcy, and a large share buyback appears unlikely soon.
Still, Morgan Stanley sees additional value in EchoStar's remaining spectrum holdings and improving credit position.
The next big test is whether SpaceX's valuation holds up long enough for that discount to become real value for EchoStar shareholders.

title: Morgan Stanley sees 45% upside in this SpaceX-linked stock
